entities.summary:
Juozas Urbšys was a prominent Lithuanian diplomat and translator who played a crucial role in shaping the country's foreign affairs during its tumultuous interwar period. As the last head of foreign affairs before Lithuania's occupation by the Soviet Union, Urbšys worked tirelessly to promote Lithuanian interests and maintain diplomatic relations with neighboring nations. His translation work also helped to preserve Lithuanian culture and language, leaving a lasting legacy for future generations.

Born in 1893, Urbšys served in the military before joining the Lithuanian Ministry of Foreign Affairs in 1918. He was appointed head of foreign affairs in 1938, a position he held until Lithuania's occupation by the Soviet Union in 1940.

Urbšys' imprisonment and deportation to Siberia had a profound impact on his life and work. Despite the harsh conditions, he continued to translate and advocate for Lithuanian causes, even while incarcerated. His dedication to his country and people earned him widespread respect and admiration.

Tragically, Urbšys died on April 30, 1991, at the age of 98, leaving behind a rich legacy as one of Lithuania's most beloved diplomats and cultural heroes.

entities.summary: Juozas Urbšys was a prominent interwar Lithuanian diplomat, the last head of foreign affairs in independent interwar Lithuania, and a translator. He served in the military between 1916 and 1922 and then joined the Lithuanian Ministry of Foreign Affairs. In 1938, Urbšys was named its head and served in that position until Lithuania's occupation in 1940. Urbšys was imprisoned by the Soviet authorities in 1940 and deported to Siberia, where he spent the next 13 years in various prisons. Urbšys died in 1991, having lived long enough to see Lithuania's independence restored, and was buried in Petrašiūnai Cemetery, Kaunas.
